chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: Moten band alumni, Eddie Durham, arrangements and stock music
summary: Basie lists men from Moten's band who later played with him and says Moten's book was fully arranged, from written parts or store-bought stock music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right. That's interesting. That's interesting. "There were some great musicians in that Moten band. Five of those musicians have played with me, right up to the present. In addition to Walter Page and Jimmy Rushing, there are Ed Lewis, my first trumpet player of long standing, Jack Washington, baritone sax and Jo Jones at the drums." We You also had such men as Eddie Durham, who played trombone. When did Eddie Durham start playing guitar?
He was playing guitar and trombone.
So he wasn't only just playing trombone, right?
"And did a great deal of the arranging."
What would he have been arranging?
What would he have been arranging?
Well, I mean, you had arrangements?
I mean, how much of the music was arranged at that time?
Well, he first started arranging with Benny Moten.
Yeah, but with Benny Moten, I mean, how much arrangements would you have had?
So that when you got with your own band, that was unlike the heads you were doing?
Yeah, that was mostly that, but --
So that you weren't getting much chance to stretch out there with that band?
Well, I mean, how much was strictly written? When you say "arranged," did you mean written?
And everything was arranged that you played or --
Not much in that (inaudible) either stock music or arrangements, dig?
Things, arrangements you can buy at the store.
